gaps: Breath one took every carrier to move ownership from the founder to the party across the table and to be agreed before it bites. Sharpening Reset with the trigger in the other hand against Stack that eats the common showed that the reset's forfeited shares are retired and lift every remaining holder pro rata, while the trigger sits with the board the investor controls: the beneficiary and the hand on the trigger are the same, and the drained party's counterparty is nobody in particular. This produced the changed question for breath two: whose hand holds the trigger, and does the same hand catch what falls.
accepted: Pool before the price: the lead requires the unallocated option pool to be enlarged before the round and counted inside the pre-money, so the pool's dilution falls entirely on the holders who were there before the money while the headline pre-money is untouched; agreed in one term-sheet line, 'pre-money includes a fifteen percent post-closing pool', understood by the lead always and by the founder when counsel explains it; with an eight million pre and two million in, a fifteen-percent post pool is one and a half million carved from the eight, so the founders' shares are priced at six and a half; not the pool itself, which real hires will need, but which side of the price line it sits on, and the tell is a pool sized to a round number rather than to a hiring plan.

Additive slices: under the post-money SAFE each check buys a percentage fixed as of the moment before the priced round and immune to every later SAFE, so the slices add and the founders alone pay for each one; agreed one check at a time with investors who never see the others, understood by the form's author, who published the arithmetic, and not by the founder who reads 'post-money' as a valuation word; five hundred thousand at a five million cap, a million at ten, a million and a half at fifteen is ten, ten, and ten percent, thirty percent gone before the Series A prices a share; not stacking as such, which pre-money notes also do while diluting one another, but immunity, which makes each slice a fixed charge on the common.

Below the threshold: grants each too small to be argued over, an advisor's quarter point, a consultant's half, a friend's tenth, are approved without the process a large grant gets and sum above the threshold the process exists for; agreed over coffee, understood by nobody as a total; six advisors at a half point each, vesting monthly with no cliff, is three percent, more than the Series A lead's board observer got for a check; not the size of any grant but the granularity that keeps each one below attention, and the tell is that nobody in the room can name the sum.

Warrant on the loan: venture debt carries warrant coverage, a fraction of the principal in warrants struck at the last round's price, so a lender who bore no equity risk holds equity if the company rises; agreed in the loan agreement and never entered on the cap table because the warrants are worth nothing the day they are struck; three million borrowed with ten-percent coverage at a ten-million post is three hundred thousand of shares at last-round price, three percent of the company on a loan that also charges twelve; not interest, which is paid in cash and ends, but a share count fixed at signing whose value waits on the exit, and the tell is a cap table that omits the debt file.

Interest that converts: a convertible note accrues interest that is never paid in cash but converts with the principal at the cap, so the dilution is a function of how long the note waits for a price; agreed as a rate everyone reads as an accounting line; two million at eight percent open for thirty months adds four hundred thousand that converts at a ten million cap into a slice of roughly four percent nobody wrote a check for; not the discount, which is fixed at signing, but a clock, and a delayed round pays for the delay in shares.

Dividend nobody pays: preferred stock carries a cumulative dividend, accruing at a stated rate and payable only at liquidation, so the preference stack grows on a clock while every financial statement shows no dividend paid; agreed as a line the founder reads as a formality because the company will never declare one, understood by the investor as a return that compounds whether or not the company does; fifty million of preferred at eight percent cumulative over five years adds twenty million to the preference before a dollar reaches common, and the sum is on no cap table; not interest that converts, which becomes shares at the next price, but a claim that stays ahead of shares until the end.

Cap as option: a valuation cap is a ceiling, not a price, so the SAFE converts at the lower of the cap and the discounted round price, and the holder is long an option whose value grows with the uncertainty of the next round; agreed when the founder treats the cap as the valuation she raised at, understood by the investor as a floor on his percentage; a SAFE at a ten million cap converts at ten if the A prices at twenty and at six if the A prices at six, so the 'ten million round' was a ten-or-less round; not a discount, which is a fixed ratio, but a payoff bent at the cap, and the tell is a founder quoting the cap as her last valuation.

Ratchet after the fact: anti-dilution resets an earlier round's conversion price when a later round prices lower, so the earlier investor receives shares as if she had bought at the lower price and the common pays for them; agreed in a clause the founder skips because she does not intend a down round, understood by the investor as the term that makes a high price safe; under a full ratchet a Series A that bought a quarter at four dollars sees a B at two and doubles its share count before the B buys a share, and broad-based weighted average softens this by the B's size; observed in Square's 2015 offering, where a Series E floor of $18.56 against a nine-dollar offer issued the E about ten million extra shares, as reported; not a repricing, which the investor did not buy, but a repricing in one direction only, so the earlier money holds a put on the later price.

Reset with the trigger in the other hand: the Series A puts a founder's already-vested shares back on a schedule with a repurchase right at cost, so a founder three years in and three-quarters vested is a quarter vested again; agreed under the sentence 'we need you committed' and understood by both sides as a commitment device, but the board that can end her employment is, after the round, a board the investor sits on, and forfeited shares are retired, which lifts every remaining holder pro rata including the one who voted; a founder with thirty percent removed twelve months after the reset keeps under half of her shares, and the seventeen percent of the company that returns is spread over whoever remains; not vesting, which any hire accepts, but a forfeiture whose trigger and beneficiary are the same hand.

Stack that eats the common: each round's preferred takes its money back before common sees anything, so the founder's percentage is a share of the exit only above the price at which conversion beats preference, and below it a good price pays the common almost nothing; agreed round by round as 'one times non-participating, standard', understood by every investor as the whole point and read by the founder as a percentage; fifty million raised at one times, exit at sixty, the preferred take fifty and a founder with twenty percent takes two million from a sale the press calls a six-fold win; not the round price, which set her percentage truly, but a floor under each round that becomes the entire payout when the exit lands near the raise, and the tell is the conversion price, above which the cap table becomes honest again.

Dip twice: participating preferred takes its preference and then its pro-rata share of what is left, so there is no exit price at which the cap table's percentage becomes the holder's share of proceeds until the participation cap is reached; agreed as one word after 'preferred', understood by the investor as the term that makes the cap table lie at every price; ten million for a quarter, exit at forty, takes ten plus a quarter of thirty, seventeen and a half, forty-four percent of the exit for twenty-five percent of the company; not the stack, which vanishes at the conversion point, but a stack with no such point below the cap, so the arithmetic must be run at every exit price rather than once.

Headline bought with terms: the investor grants the valuation the founder needs for the press, the hires, and the next round, and takes it back in the waterfall, so the price is real in one ledger and false in the other; agreed with both parties knowing and each believing the other's ledger is the one that will not matter; twenty million for twenty percent at a hundred post with one-times participating pays the investor forty-six million on a hundred-and-fifty exit, while twenty million for twenty-nine percent at seventy post with one-times non-participating pays forty-three, so the higher valuation was the dearer one; adds to what-a-price-does' price for the stranger's eyes the compensating term that makes the stranger's number cheap for the party who granted it; not a bad price but a price paid in a currency the price does not show.

Ten votes a share: the founder's class carries ten votes, so control is conserved while economics drain, and the leak is in the sunset and the transfer clauses, since the class converts to common on sale, on death, on leaving, or on a date; agreed at incorporation or at the offering, understood by the founder as permanent and by counsel as a schedule; eight percent of the economics with fifty-five percent of the vote, until a divorce transfers a block that converts on transfer and the vote falls under half; not control as such but control on a clock the founder does not see as a clock, and the tell is that the class's conversion events are listed on a page she never turned to.

Veto without votes: protective provisions give the preferred a class vote over a sale, a new round, debt, the budget, and the pool, so a twenty-percent holder can block anything while the cap table shows nothing, since the control lives in the charter and not in the count; agreed as 'standard protective provisions', understood by the investor as the deal and by the founder as boilerplate; the reverse of ten votes a share, economics intact and control gone, and a board seat granted to a two-percent seed holder is the same carrier held by a body instead of a class; not a majority but a list of things a majority may not do, and no arithmetic ever shows it.

residue.item: Tranche as free call: a round paid in milestone tranches at a fixed price, so the investor holds a call on the second tranche and walks if the milestone fails.
residue.why: Rejected: what moves is the investor's option on uncommitted money, and its drain is the headline price of the second tranche, which is out by the item type; its control half, who judges the milestone, is carried by Veto without votes.

residue.item: Seat that does not dilute: a board seat granted to a seed investor that persists after dilution to two percent.
residue.why: Merged into Veto without votes as the same carrier held by a body instead of a class; no separate arithmetic and no separate moment of agreement.

residue.item: Cram-down: a recapitalization that sets the pre-money near zero against the old preference stack.
residue.why: Rejected: the carrier is the price itself, agreed by every party in the room on the day; the item type excludes drains that run through the headline price, and the boundary case records it.

residue.item: Maturity's hand: a convertible note's maturity date, on which the holder becomes a creditor who can call a loan the company cannot pay and extract a lower cap.
residue.why: Held, then rejected: the drain runs through a renegotiated cap, which is the conversion price, and the lever is a creditor's hold of the kind who-can-be-bound already maps under Tap; the clock half survives as Interest that converts.

residue.item: Escrow and earnout: a headline acquisition price of which a third is held back and a fifth is contingent on targets the acquirer controls.
residue.why: Rejected: it drains consideration and time, not ownership or control; a price-shape and lead-time mechanism, not a carrier of shares or vetoes.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored analytical fieldwork over standard-form instruments (venture term sheets, the post-money SAFE, venture loan warrants, option plans, protective provisions, dual-class charters), each simplified to one mechanism; not a legal or tax guide, and jurisdiction, plan design, and negotiation change several of them.
The arithmetic is illustrative in round numbers and belongs to no company; the single documented case, Square's 2015 ratchet, is cited as reported and not analyzed from filings.

The claims about who understood a term at signing describe a typical asymmetry the author asserts, not a finding; a founder with counsel who reads the documents can understand every carrier here, and the map does not claim otherwise.

The itinerary sorts by what the carrier's amount waits on, not by the size or frequency of the drain; no claim of exhaustiveness, and carriers where the headline price is itself the route (a recap, a cram-down, a low seed price) are out by the item type.

Adjacent admitted items and what ours add: Headline bought with terms adds to what-a-price-does' Price for the stranger's eyes the compensating term; Ratchet after the fact runs the opposite way from clean-exits' Fade by formula, since the price rather than the holder pulls it and the preferred gains; Ninety-day guillotine is the exit-door toll on the asset runway-illusions' Reach the cliff describes arriving; Veto without votes is live legal power, not ghost-leverages' habit.

gaps: The changed question yielded carriers that return ownership to the company rather than to a counterparty (Ninety-day guillotine, joining the reset), a carrier that moves a claim without moving a share (Secondary that grows the stack), and a carrier agreed at the moment it bites by the party it pays (Carve-out at the door). The territory pointer 'dilution carriers' stands and the slug is kept, but the of-sentence now names control as a thing that drains without arithmetic and the itinerary ends on it. The brief's live question, which carriers a spreadsheet shows at signing and which only at exit, became the seriation axis, with two stages the question did not anticipate: a person's leaving, and the room at the exit where the carve-out is agreed.
accepted: Ninety-day guillotine: vested options must be exercised within ninety days of leaving, paying the strike and the tax on the spread, or they lapse back to the pool, so the carrier of an employee's ownership back to the company is a purchase price on the exit door, due on the day she can least afford it; agreed in the plan document every hire signs unread, written by counsel under a tax rule; fifty thousand vested options at a two-dollar strike against a twenty-dollar appraisal is a hundred thousand in cash and a nine-hundred-thousand spread the tax bill can treat as income, so a departing engineer with a mortgage forfeits ownership she spent four years earning; not a vesting term, since the shares had vested, but a toll on keeping them, and what lapses returns pro rata to the holders who stayed.

Secondary that grows the stack: a buyer of founder or early-holder common in a secondary demands the shares be reclassified into the latest preferred, so a preference is created on shares that carried none, the stack grows by the secondary's size, and no cash reaches the company; agreed between seller and buyer, understood by the buyer's counsel, and invisible to the employees, since nothing was issued; a founder who sells five million of common at the Series C price adds five million to the stack ahead of the shares she kept and ahead of everyone's options; not the sale itself, which moves ownership at a price, but the reclassification, which moves a claim.

Carve-out at the door: when the exit price sits inside the stack, the preferred agree a management carve-out, a share of proceeds paid to named, still-employed executives before the waterfall, so the same founder is paid as a manager and nothing as a shareholder, and every common holder who left gets nothing; agreed at the exit, by the board, understood by the board and by no one who has already gone; a hundred-million sale against a hundred and twenty of preference with a ten-percent carve-out pays ten million to the four managers named and zero to two hundred option holders and the departed co-founder; not the stack, which is the cause, but the exception bought from it, and it forks the founder from the people who built the thing with her.

residue.item: Pro rata that isn't: super pro rata rights that enlarge the round beyond what the founder agreed, so someone without the right must absorb the enlargement.
residue.why: Rejected: the enlargement is dilution at the round price, so the route is the headline price; what it adds, that every immunity is a charge on whoever lacks one, is stated once in the seriation note as the conservation law rather than as an item.

residue.item: Acceleration on change of control: unvested shares that vest on acquisition, single or double trigger.
residue.why: Rejected: it moves ownership toward the employee and out of the acquirer's retention budget, a carrier in the opposite direction; held for a map of what an exit gives rather than takes.

residue.item: Strike set by appraisal: the option strike fixed at the 409A value so that the spread is taxed at departure.
residue.why: Merged into Ninety-day guillotine as the arithmetic of the toll; it is the same door and the same day.

residue.item: Founder loan for exercise: a company loan to a departing holder to pay the strike.
residue.why: Rejected: a remedy for the guillotine, not a carrier; it moves nothing by itself.

neighbors.left: Stack that eats the common: each round's preferred takes its money back before common sees anything, so the founder's percentage is a share of the exit only above the price at which conversion beats preference, and below it a good price pays the common almost nothing; agreed round by round as 'one times non-participating, standard', understood by every investor as the whole point and read by the founder as a percentage; fifty million raised at one times, exit at sixty, the preferred take fifty and a founder with twenty percent takes two million from a sale the press calls a six-fold win; not the round price, which set her percentage truly, but a floor under each round that becomes the entire payout when the exit lands near the raise, and the tell is the conversion price, above which the cap table becomes honest again.
neighbors.right: Dip twice: participating preferred takes its preference and then its pro-rata share of what is left, so there is no exit price at which the cap table's percentage becomes the holder's share of proceeds until the participation cap is reached; agreed as one word after 'preferred', understood by the investor as the term that makes the cap table lie at every price; ten million for a quarter, exit at forty, takes ten plus a quarter of thirty, seventeen and a half, forty-four percent of the exit for twenty-five percent of the company; not the stack, which vanishes at the conversion point, but a stack with no such point below the cap, so the arithmetic must be run at every exit price rather than once.
neighbors.separating_case: Fifty million raised, a founder holding twenty percent, and an exit at five hundred million. Under a one-times non-participating stack every series converts, the stack vanishes, and the founder's twenty percent is a hundred million, so above the conversion point the cap table told the truth. Under participating preferred with no cap the same investors take their fifty and a share of the four hundred and fifty besides, so the founder's twenty percent is a share of proceeds at no exit price at all. The existence of a price at which the cap table becomes honest separates them, and it is the number an operator should ask for.

checks.boundary_case: A low round price is out: the founder who sold forty percent at the seed because she had two months of cash was drained by the headline price, which everyone at the table computed on the day. A recapitalization is out for the same reason, since the pre-money set near zero against forty million of old preference is a price, and the drain runs through it and not around it. Cap as option is in on exactly that contrast, because the cap is read as the price and is not one.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the itinerary conceals: Pool before the price → Below the threshold → Pool before the price, where grants drawn from a pool the founders paid for are refilled inside the next pre-money, and Ratchet after the fact → Pool before the price enters the same loop from the next-price stage, since a down round refills the pool as well. It shows a passage between levels at Interest that converts → Dividend nobody pays, where the same clock that accrued shares at the note level accrues preference at the exit level. It shows a fork at Stack that eats the common → Carve-out at the door, where one exit price splits the common into the paid and the unpaid along the line of who is still employed, which the cap table cannot express. It shows a same-hand coupling at Reset with the trigger in the other hand → Ninety-day guillotine, two carriers that the sequence places as neighbors and the edge shows firing from a single decision whose maker catches what falls. And it shows an incompatibility at Ten votes a share → Veto without votes, where the two control carriers, placed together at the end of the itinerary, cancel into a stalemate rather than adding.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a distinct carrier, the moment it is agreed, and an arithmetic that a different input unlocks; the strange members (a reset whose beneficiary is the hand on the trigger, a secondary that creates a claim without issuing a share, a carve-out agreed at the moment it bites) are kept as mechanisms and not softened into advice to read the documents.

next_crossfield_opening: Carriers that return what falls to the company: connect Reset with the trigger in the other hand and Ninety-day guillotine with clean-exits' Fade by formula and witness-architectures' Silence priced as guilt; ask which forfeitures are priced as options by the party who holds the trigger, and whether a forfeiture whose beneficiary is everyone pro rata can be negotiated by anyone at all.
